lead.tldr: Security risk: DPRK-linked heists net $578M, indicating heightened nation‑state targeting of DeFi protocols • Private key compromises cost $8.5bn and hiring dedicated security officers could become a new operational standard • UK Treasury’s stablecoin and tokenisation bill positions London as a regulated hub, likely attracting institutional capital • Strategy’s STRC preferred equity offers 11.5% dividend but dividend suspension risk makes it speculative for risk‑averse investors • ABTC’s addition of 11,000 rigs boosts hash‑rate, signaling continued mining profitability despite rising energy scrutiny • Uzbekistan’s Karakalpakstan mining zone offers cheap power and tax breaks, likely drawing foreign mining operators

intro: Dear Founders, Investors, and Friends, today we see North Korean‑linked heists exposing security gaps, the UK rolling out a stablecoin regulatory framework, and ABTC powering up 11,000 new Bitcoin miners. These events highlight both risk and growth in the ecosystem.

top_signals.title: North Korea Tied to Heists Worth $578M in April After Kelp DAO Exploit
top_signals.summary: In April, actors linked to North Korea executed two major crypto thefts, taking a total of $578 million from the Kelp DAO exploit and the Drift decentralized exchange. The operations demonstrate that DPRK cyber groups are expanding tactics to include in‑person social engineering at industry conferences. The incidents coincide with an increase in crypto‑crime complaints to the FBI, underscoring heightened regulatory and security risks for institutional participants in digital assets.

top_signals.title: Justin Sun says he's suing Trump's $2.5bn crypto project over frozen WLFI tokens
top_signals.summary: Tron founder Justin Sun has filed a lawsuit against World Liberty Financial, a cryptocurrency project linked to former President Donald Trump. Sun alleges that the project froze approximately $75 million worth of his WLFI voting tokens. The legal action follows a previous settlement with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission involving the same token. WLFI’s market value has fallen 76 percent from its peak, leaving the project with a market cap of about $2.5 billion, a decline that raises concerns for institutional investors about governance and regulatory risk.

top_signals.title: UK government bets on stablecoins and tokenisation to drive fintech growth
top_signals.summary: The UK Treasury has introduced a package of regulatory measures targeting stablecoins and tokenised payment systems. The package includes a new crypto bill that sets out rules for digital asset issuers and a dedicated wholesale digital markets champion to oversee implementation. By establishing clear oversight, the government seeks to attract fintech firms and institutional investors to the UK’s digital asset ecosystem. The approach balances the ambition to become a leading hub for digital assets with the need to protect consumers.

top_signals.title: ABTC Energizes More Than 11,000 New Bitcoin Mining Rigs
top_signals.summary: ABTC has brought more than 11,000 new Bitcoin mining rigs online, boosting its hash‑rate capacity. This addition reflects ongoing expansion in the Bitcoin mining industry. Institutional investors may view the increased hash‑rate as a signal of scaling operational efficiency and potential impact on network security.

top_signals.title: Crypto’s biggest selling point is responsible for $8.5bn in losses. But it can be made safe
top_signals.summary: Private key compromises have resulted in $8.5 bn of crypto losses, highlighting the security challenges of self‑custody for investors. The magnitude of these losses underscores why self‑custody, often promoted as crypto’s biggest selling point, remains a risk factor for institutional portfolios. Cybersecurity specialist David Schwed contends that employing dedicated security officers and upgrading infrastructure can mitigate those risks. He points to recent DeFi hacks on Drift and Kelp DAO as evidence that weak security practices, not the self‑custody model itself, drive the losses.

top_signals.title: Everyone is frothing about Bitcoin treasury company Strategy’s STRC bond. Should they be?
top_signals.summary: Strategy’s STRC preferred equity is a high‑yield security backed by Bitcoin that offers an 11.5% dividend and has attracted strong investor demand. The product is positioned as a treasury‑style vehicle that provides Bitcoin exposure without direct ownership, appealing to institutions seeking yield in a low‑rate environment. Analysts caution that dividend payments can be suspended and the underlying Bitcoin exposure remains speculative, suggesting the current enthusiasm may be temporary.

top_signals.title: Kalshi Selects Pyth to Set Prices for Commodities Trades
top_signals.summary: Kalshi, a regulated derivatives exchange, has chosen the Pyth network to serve as the price oracle for its commodities contracts. The partnership will provide real‑time, tamper‑proof price data across a range of commodity assets. Institutional investors can expect improved market integrity and more reliable pricing inputs for risk management and compliance.

top_signals.title: 주식·암호화폐·베팅이 한 곳으로: 폴리마켓 무기한 선물 거래 출시로 엿볼 수 있는 미래
top_signals.summary: Polymarket and Kalshi have introduced perpetual futures that cover assets including cryptocurrencies, commodities and equities such as Nvidia. The products are expected to obtain regulatory approval, signaling compliance with existing financial frameworks. This launch illustrates a growing industry shift toward unified platforms that combine stock trading, crypto exposure and prediction markets, a model first popularized by Robinhood and relevant for institutional portfolio diversification.

top_signals.title: One Platform, All Assets: What Polymarket’s Perpetuals Launch Reveals
top_signals.summary: Polymarket and Kalshi have announced a joint launch of perpetual futures contracts that will span crypto assets, commodities and equities. The new product line is designed to provide a single trading interface for multiple asset classes, echoing the multi‑asset approach popularized by platforms such as Robinhood. By consolidating disparate markets onto one platform, the initiative aims to attract institutional participants seeking streamlined execution and risk management. The expansion is expected to become a significant growth driver for both firms once they secure the necessary regulatory approvals.

top_signals.title: Stratiphy Restores Crypto ETN Access for UK Investors via New ISA Offering
top_signals.summary: Stratiphy has launched a new Individual Savings Account (ISA) product that re‑enables UK retail investors to purchase crypto exchange‑traded notes (ETNs). The offering restores a pathway that had been unavailable after previous regulatory restrictions. It aligns with the Financial Conduct Authority’s ongoing development of a crypto regulatory framework. The move is viewed as a signal of increasing compliance and could support broader market growth for crypto‑linked products.

top_signals.title: Uzbekistan Launches Crypto Mining Zone in Karakalpakstan
top_signals.summary: Uzbekistan has announced the establishment of a dedicated cryptocurrency mining zone in the autonomous republic of Karakalpakstan. The government plans to offer incentives such as low‑cost electricity to mining operators. Tax breaks are also part of the incentive package to attract foreign investment. The initiative aims to position Uzbekistan as a regional hub for crypto mining and to draw institutional capital into the sector.

linkedin_post: Dear Founders, Investors, and Friends, The past month reminded us why vigilance, governance and clear regulation are essential in the crypto ecosystem. In April, actors linked to North Korea carried out two high‑profile thefts that together drained $578 million from the Kelp DAO exploit and the Drift DEX. The attacks were not only technical, they included in‑person social engineering at industry events, highlighting a new layer of threat that institutional participants must anticipate. At the same time, the legal landscape is evolving. Tron founder Justin Sun has filed a lawsuit against World Liberty Financial, a project associated with former President Donald Trump, alleging that the platform froze $75 million of his WLFI voting tokens. The dispute follows a prior settlement with the SEC and underscores the importance of robust token governance and regulatory compliance for projects seeking institutional backing. On a more positive note, the UK Treasury has unveiled a regulatory package that puts stablecoins and tokenised payment systems on a clear legal footing. By introducing a dedicated crypto bill and appointing a wholesale digital markets champion, the government aims to attract fintech innovators and institutional capital while protecting consumers. For us at Blockwall, these developments reinforce the need to back founders who prioritize security, transparent governance and alignment with emerging regulatory frameworks.
